summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, chronic diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and diabetes was admitted due to symptomatic hypotension following hemodialysis. She presented with fatigue and a blood pressure of 62/34 mmHg, requiring fluid resuscitation and placement of a femoral central venous catheter. The hypotension was attributed to excessive fluid removal during dialysis and the cumulative effects of multiple antihypertensive medications. Cardiac biomarkers were elevated, but no acute coronary syndrome was found; findings were consistent with subendocardial ischemia due to low perfusion. Medications were adjusted, including dose reductions in metoprolol and verapamil, and discontinuation of lisinopril, valsartan, and isosorbide mononitrate. Calcium acetate was stopped due to hypophosphatemia. She remained hemodynamically stable, completed dialysis without complications, and was discharged home asymptomatic with updated medication instructions and close follow-up plans.
